name: Skeleton
summary: A placeholder shape that stands in for content while it loads.
description: A skeleton draws the outline of content that is not there yet: a line of text, an avatar, a card. Several skeletons laid out like the content they stand for tell people what is coming and where, with less jump than a spinner followed by the real content. A skeleton is invisible to assistive technology; the region that loads says so itself.

anatomy.description: Root: the shape itself, hidden from assistive technology. Carries the shape; width and height are the content it stands for.

properties.name: Shape
properties.description: What the placeholder stands for; sets the corners and the default height.

options.description: A line of text: full width, 16 px high, slightly rounded.
An avatar or an icon: a 40 px disc.
A block (an image, a card): full width, 96 px high, 8 px corners.

properties.name: Width
properties.description: Width of the shape as a CSS length or percentage (60%, 12rem); the content's width. Full width by default, or the height for a circle.

properties.name: Height
properties.description: Height of the shape as a CSS length; the content's height. The shape's default otherwise.

states.description: The only state: the shape pulses while it is shown.

notes: A skeleton takes the size given to it, or the shape's default; the layout places skeletons as it will place the content.
A text skeleton is one line: stack several, the last one shorter, for a paragraph.

name.text: A skeleton has no name and no role: it is hidden from assistive technology. The loading region names what is happening, with a status message or by being marked busy.

guidelines.text: A skeleton is pure decoration standing in for content: it is implemented so assistive technology ignores it, it carries no text, and the structure it sketches is conveyed by the content once loaded, and by the loading region's status meanwhile.

Render each shape with aria-hidden="true". Mark the region that loads with aria-busy="true" while the skeletons show, and announce the loading and the arrival of the content with a status message when the wait is long.
The shapes convey nothing by themselves (1.12:1 and 1.21:1 against the default surface): the layout of the skeletons, not their color, says what is coming. They never carry information people need.

The pulse is a gentle opacity change, stopped when the user asks for reduced motion; skeletons disappear as soon as the content arrives, so they are never a long-running animation next to other content.
Reduce automatic animations when Reduce Motion is on.
Pass null as the contentDescription of placeholder graphics so they are not communicated.

references.title: Jetpack Compose accessibility: graphic elements (contentDescription null for decoration)
MDN: aria-busy (an element being modified or loading)
Understanding WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (a preloader animation example)

guidelines: A skeleton carries no text. The loading region's status message says what loads: Loading your projects.

decisions.text: A skeleton is filled with the Figma library's skeleton state color (global.bg.state.skeleton.default, translucent) and pulses between fully opaque and the 50 % opacity step, six times the normal duration per half cycle.
Three shapes with default sizes from the space scale: text (16 px high, 2 px corners), circle (40 px, fully round) and rectangle (96 px high, 8 px corners); width and height are the consumer's.
A skeleton is hidden from assistive technology; the loading region is marked busy and announces the loading with a status message.

changelog.note: Initial draft (decisions skeleton-fill, shapes, hidden-from-assistive-technology). A hidden pulsing shape in three shapes with consumer sizes; no interaction state. Fill measured only: 1.12 (light) and 1.21 (dark) against the default surface.
